payload.analysis: 结合外伤后皮肤感染的推测，组织病理见真皮及皮下坏死伴致密混合炎细胞浸润、血管坏死闭塞，PAS见大量薄壁分隔菌丝，真菌培养及序列分析符合致病真菌，支持植物外伤后真菌性皮肤感染；Fontana-Masson无色素不支持产黑色素真菌。活检未见恶性证据，但细菌培养和深部影像未获取，不能完全排除混合感染或深部累及。关键真菌学信息已覆盖。

why.why: Laboratory and pathology analyses now show angioinvasive septate hyphae in vessel lumens and culture-confirmed filamentous fungus with appressoria, in a patient with plant trauma and corticosteroid immunosuppression. This establishes post-trauma skin infection as the leading diagnosis and explains the necrotic purulent ulcer. Confidence is raised from 0.45 to 0.85; mixed bacterial infection or deep extension cannot be fully excluded because bacterial culture and deep imaging were not obtained.

payload.analysis: Biopsy and culture confirm angioinvasive septate hyphae and a filamentous fungus with appressoria, establishing post-traumatic fungal skin infection as the leading diagnosis. Plant trauma and corticosteroid use support this. Malignancy and primary inflammatory ulcer are refuted by histology. However, bacterial co-infection and deep extension remain unexcluded because bacterial culture and lower extremity imaging were not obtained; these are key missing pieces for complete verification.

payload.analysis: Combined with the belief of post-traumatic angioinvasive fungal infection, histology shows necrotic vessel occlusion with septate hyphae, PAS confirms hyphae in vessel lumens, Fontana-Masson negativity rules out pigmented fungi, and culture with appressoria plus ITS sequencing identifies a filamentous fungus, strongly supporting the diagnosis. Bacterial co-infection and deep extension remain unassessed because bacterial culture and MRI/CT were not performed; all available key imaging and pathology information is covered, and clinical follow-up for these residual uncertainties is recommended.

payload.report: Post-traumatic angioinvasive fungal infection explains the right lower leg swelling. Evidence: plant trauma, immunosuppression, necrotic ulcers, biopsy with septate hyphae and vascular occlusion, PAS-positive non-melanized hyphae, culture-confirmed fungus with appressoria. This refutes malignancy and inflammatory ulcer; infected venous stasis ulcer is less likely. Missing bacterial culture and MRI/CT leave secondary bacterial infection and deep extension possible but unconfirmed.
